clue.text: Constituents of fat MP — he is no longer important

indicators.note: the letters of the next words are treated as raw ingredients to be put together afresh

explanation.surface: An overweight MP has lost his seat and his standing with his constituents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constituents' looks like an MP's voters, but it is the anagram signal, and the first word stands unscrambled at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone off the map has dropped out of notice, an idiom for faded importance.

clue.text: Stretch limo a feature of award ceremony

parts.note: OS is outsize, the extra-large sense of a stretch limo
a limousine is a car

explanation.surface: A stretch limo pulling up at an awards night.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oscar statuette is the prize handed out at the Academy Awards.

clue.text: Pardoning quartet caught in criminal act

indicators.note: the number is trapped inside the crime word

parts.note: forging is counterfeiting, a crime
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four people caught in the act are let off.
explanation.definitionFit: Forgiving means pardoning, letting off a wrong.

clue.text: Man has let in competing players for autumnal celebration

indicators.note: the permission word is put inside the man word, as 'has ... in' says

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
to let is to allow
E, East, is one of the four players at the bridge table
N, North, is another bridge player, opposing East

explanation.surface: A man lets competing players into his autumn party.
explanation.walkthrough: At bridge the four players are North, South, East and West; East and North are on opposing sides, so competing.
explanation.definitionFit: Halloween, 31 October, is the autumn festival of the eve of All Saints.

clue.text: Crown avoiding extremes

definitions.meaning: the crown of a road is its raised centre line
moderate, of views that keep away from either wing

explanation.definitionFit: A road's crown is its centre, and moderate politics is called the centre ground.

clue.text: Make an effort and show a leg? On the contrary

definitions.meaning: try harder, the idiom of hauling up hosiery

definitions.text: show a leg? On the contrary
definitions.meaning: drawing hosiery upward covers the leg rather than revealing it

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means try harder, and literally the act hides the shins, opposite of showing a leg.

clue.text: Lovely girl has left scene of confusion

parts.note: a babe is slang for an attractive young woman

explanation.surface: An attractive girl has walked out of a chaotic scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tower of Babel in Genesis was where tongues were confused, so the name stands for uproar.

clue.text: Like a bat in the shade

definitions.meaning: sightless, as in the phrase ... as a bat
a window screen that pulls down

explanation.definitionFit: Bats are proverbially sightless, and a window shade is a roller screen.

clue.text: Indulge too much — contents of wine store, for instance, brought up

parts.note: a bin is a rack where wine is kept

indicators.note: in a down entry the example abbreviation is raised, so read upwards

parts.note: EG, exempli gratia, means for instance

explanation.surface: Someone overdoes it, bringing up the contents of the wine store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contents of' joins the store to what it holds; the bin is the store itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To binge is to overindulge in a bout of eating or drinking.

clue.text: Indolent lady — here pepper-and-salt might put in an appearance

definitions.meaning: a lazy woman with the name Susan

definitions.text: here pepper-and-salt might put in an appearance
definitions.meaning: a rotating tray brings condiments round the table

explanation.definitionFit: A revolving tray on a dining table, which brings condiments round to each diner.

clue.text: Anger about class entered in record and highlighted with pen?

indicators.note: the anger-and-class group is put into the record, so 'entered in' marks a container

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc, a kind of record

indicators.note: the anger word goes round the class abbreviation, as 'about' means surrounding

parts.note: ire is a literary word for anger
CL is an abbreviation for class

explanation.surface: Someone furious about their class gets it noted on file and underlined in pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringing a word with a pen is a way of marking it out, hence the question mark for the loose sense.

clue.text: Note that's kept back by Bess, a philosopher

indicators.note: the reversed note letters are held inside the name, so 'kept ... by' marks a container

parts.note: Bess and Liz are both pet forms of Elizabeth

indicators.note: the note and 'that is' letters are read backwards

parts.note: NB, nota bene, is a note telling the reader to mark something
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A note is held back by a woman called Bess, who turns out to be a thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bess' is a pet form of Elizabeth, and so is the shorter name that does the holding here; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Gottfried Leibniz was a German philosopher and mathematician who co-invented the calculus.

clue.text: Cash letter from abroad has enclosed within

indicators.note: the Greek letter holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet
in is a synonym of within

explanation.surface: Money arrives in a foreign letter with something tucked inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhino is old British slang for money.

clue.text: City strip is cleaner

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
to strip is to undress

explanation.surface: A city statement that stripping is cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A laundress washes clothes for a living, a cleaner of linen.

clue.text: Bung cheese round top of bun

indicators.note: the cheese goes around the next letter

parts.note: brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: the first letter of the word bun is taken

explanation.surface: A recipe: wrap cheese round the top of a bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bung' is British slang for a bribe as well as a stopper.
explanation.definitionFit: Bung is British slang for an illicit payment made to secure favour.

clue.text: Encouraged to get out earlier, being physically challenged

indicators.note: the dismissal word comes before the encouragement word

parts.note: to bowl a batsman in cricket is to get him out
egged, as in egged on, means urged

explanation.surface: Urged to dismiss a batsman early despite some handicap.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a bowler who hits the stumps bowls the batsman out.
explanation.definitionFit: Bow-legged describes legs bent outward, a physical condition.

clue.text: Rouses old hurt, though not raising a stink

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are damaged and come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Something stirs up old wounds without making a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stink' reads as a fuss but is meant literally, a smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Without any smell at all, the literal sense of making no stink.

clue.text: Soak in running water English dog

parts.note: to ret flax is to soak it

indicators.note: the English abbreviation goes inside the river

parts.note: a river is running water

explanation.surface: An English dog soaking in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A retriever is a gun dog breed bred to fetch shot game.

clue.text: Two participants in film overlap, portraying dentist

parts.note: an extra is a background player in a film

indicators.note: the two film words share a letter, so one copy where they join is dropped

parts.note: an actor is a performer in a film

explanation.surface: Two film performers overlap in a scene playing a dentist.
explanation.walkthrough: EXTRA and ACTOR share the A where they meet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dentist pulls teeth, so is jocularly an extractor.

clue.text: Pay packet contains nothing after deduction for tax and transport

indicators.note: the pay word holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: a wage is the pay in a weekly packet
O looks like zero, nothing
nett is pay after tax is taken off

explanation.surface: A pay packet left with nothing once tax and travel are deducted.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagonette is a horse-drawn four-wheeled carriage, a vehicle for transport.

clue.text: Atlas, possibly — it's been bound in brown

indicators.note: the pronoun is wrapped up inside the colour word

parts.note: tan is a light brown
the word it, with 's standing for has

explanation.surface: An atlas, perhaps, bound in brown leather.
explanation.walkthrough: The atlas is not a book but the Greek giant who held up the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlas was one of the Titans of Greek myth, so he is an example of the class.

clue.text: Pint seems to be poured out in a vacuum

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are tipped out and recombined

explanation.surface: A pint seems to vanish when poured into empty space.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacuum is space with nothing in it, the state of being empty.

clue.text: Dad left Mum some capital

parts.note: pa is a word for father
ma is a word for mother

explanation.surface: Dad has left Mum a nest egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Palma is the capital of Majorca, one of many capitals.

clue.text: Admitted in the wrong order? One's up the creek here

indicators.note: the letters of the synonym are jumbled

parts.note: let in means admitted

explanation.surface: A rule-breaker admits being up the creek.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlet is a narrow arm of water, a creek, so a boat could be up it.

clue.text: Sarah's son has two different accounts

parts.note: an ISA is an individual savings account
AC is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: Sarah's boy keeps money in two separate accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: ISA is a British tax-free individual savings account.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Isaac is the son born to Abraham and Sarah.

clue.text: Younger son acted badly

indicators.note: the word acted is performed poorly, its letters messed up

explanation.surface: A younger son puts on a poor performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadet is the old term for a younger son of a family.

clue.text: Astronomer, girl attached to one particular constellation

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
I is the Roman numeral one
Leo, the lion, is one named constellation

explanation.surface: A star-gazer with a girl who is attached to a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo Galilei was the Italian who turned the telescope on the heavens.

clue.text: Wanted by firm — surgeon and journalist

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a vet is a veterinary surgeon
ED is the abbreviation for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A company seeks a surgeon and a journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: To covet is to desire eagerly, so the past form means wanted.

clue.text: Send medical officer to the rear

parts.note: DR, doctor, is a medical man
aft means at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: An order to post the medical officer to the back lines.
explanation.definitionFit: To draft is to detail or dispatch people, as troops sent to a post.

clue.text: Fighting man restarted after break

indicators.note: the word restarted is broken up and its letters reset

explanation.surface: A soldier starts again after a pause in the fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: DESERT RATS were the British 7th Armoured Division in North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A Desert Rat was a soldier of the 7th Armoured Division in the Second World War.
